records.subject: Thermal expansion in light ionic crystals LiH and NaH
records.object: Lattice thermal conductivity reduction of approximately 40%
records.quote: Combining first-principles calculations with quasiharmonic approximation and Boltzmann transport equation we take light ionic crystals LiH and NaH as examples to systematically investigate the lattice thermal properties.
context_quotes: Remarkably, thermal expansion (TE) effect plays a significant role in heat transport of these light solids, which makes the lattice thermal conductivity K-L reduce about 40% compared with the value excluding the TE effect.
modality_evidence: Combining first-principles calculations with quasiharmonic approximation and Boltzmann transport equation we take light ionic crystals LiH and NaH as examples to systematically investigate the lattice thermal properties.
records.conditions: LiH and NaH; compared with excluding thermal expansion; first-principles calculations with quasiharmonic approximation and Boltzmann transport equation

records.subject: LiH
records.object: Calculated lattice thermal conductivity 14.67 W m−1 K−1 at 300 K and 12.98 W m−1 K−1 at 327 K
records.quote: Combining first-principles calculations with quasiharmonic approximation and Boltzmann transport equation we take light ionic crystals LiH and NaH as examples to systematically investigate the lattice thermal properties.
context_quotes: Remarkably, thermal expansion (TE) effect plays a significant role in heat transport of these light solids, which makes the lattice thermal conductivity K-L reduce about 40% compared with the value excluding the TE effect.
